messages:
anya: Heads-up: Customer X reported p99 spikes on hosted generate in eu-west-1 starting ~03:20 UTC. Correlated with prefix/KV cache miss rate jumping from ~2% to ~38%.
mike: Grafana: https://graf.redwood/prod/eu/g/kv-metrics?panelId=42&from=3282023500&to=3282024400 - shows tail latency and miss-rate aligned. Key metric: `prefix_cache_miss_total`.
support-agent: Escalation ticket #8472 created. Customer says regressions began after last-night model rollout; they have `redwood-7b-q4ab` pinned.
anya: Repro we ran locally: `curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -d '{"input":"hello"}'` -> headers: `X-Cache: MISS` ~35% of the time. Can share sample payloads.
suman: Pulled logs from inference host: `cache_key="user:prefix:TenantID:SessionID"` - seeing inconsistent normalization. Some keys have trailing spaces and uppercase hex tenant IDs.
mike: That would explode effective key cardinality -> no reuse -> warmup thrash. Can someone grep commit history touching prefix key formation? This looks like a normalization regression.
lina: Will check service shim. Last PR touching cache key path was #2394 (hash compatibility change). I’ll run `git blame` on the generation shim.
sre-bot: Alert created: INC-2026-03-17-412 - p99 spike eu-west-1. Pager duty notified.
mike: Short-term mitigation: route affected customer traffic to fallback cluster `redwood-7b-q4ab-v1` (older revision) and set `max_prefetch=0` to avoid re-warm storms. We can do via Console routing override for that tenant.
anya: Support plan: @lina, please coordinate the route override and memcache pool bump. I'll prepare a KB note for the customer explaining the mitigation.
suman: Fix idea: apply normalization before hashing: `key = key.strip().lower()` and remove debug-only request ids from prefix key. Also cap per-tenant prefix cardinality (e.g., 50k) with LRU window. I have a branch with tests reproducing the miss pattern.
mike: Also noticed cache eviction algorithm on hot shards is CLOCK with a big window; hotspots persist. Suggest switching to segmented LRU for hot shards to prioritize frequently-accessed prefixes. That needs a cache restart on the service but should be low-risk in canary.
lina: If we need immediate relief without deploys we can increase memcache pool in eu-west-1 by +20% for 2 hours and throttle prefetching.
support-agent: :thumbsup: Updating ticket #8472 with current mitigation steps. Asking customer for an example payload and timestamp that triggered MISS.
ya: typo aside
anya: Action items summary: 1) @suman open PR for key normalization + unit tests (ETA 4h). 2) @mike run canary for cache eviction change/config (ETA 2h). 3) @lina perform route override + temporary pool bump (now). 4) @support-agent get customer sample payloads and confirm improvement.
suman: Working on PR now. Found secondary leak: debug header `X-Req-ID` was appended into cache key in 2% of code paths. Removing that fixes a bunch of churn in my local sim.
mike: Let's also add observability: `prefix_key_normalized_total`, `prefix_cardinality_per_tenant` and a per-tenant miss-rate alert so we catch future regressions earlier.
sre-bot: Incident severity set to HIGH. Thread pinned.
lina: Done with route override and memcache bump. Customer reported p99 drop ~12% at 03:45 UTC after the change; monitoring continues.
support-agent: Customer replied: "Thanks, saw improvement — will monitor for 1 hour." We offered to run an A/B with older revision if they want sustained relief.
anya: Good progress. Keep notes in the incident doc and add postmortem items: root cause = key normalization regression + debug-id leak; mitigations = normalization patch, eviction algo change, better metrics/alerts, and shorter-term pool bump/route fallback.
support-agent: Will close loop with customer once PR is deployed to canary and stable metrics hold for 24h.
